gaps.text: In-line measurement of Turbidity / optical scattering state with turbidity sensor or the spectral scatter signal itself
In-line measurement of Process temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: start with one PLS model per method, then join synchronised NIR and Raman spectra or scores with block scaling. Both probes must sample the same spot and the data must be normalised to a common time step. The fused model must beat the best single-method model on held-out batches, otherwise the Raman instrument is dropped.)
Protein detection limits or accuracy achievable in whey specifically; no source gives figures for this matrix.

items.finding: The text notes that the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands represents a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, requiring tempered sample holders.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests that temperature fluctuations in the dairy whey stream should be carefully monitored or controlled during NIR measurements to avoid thermal interference with water bands.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source discusses biopharmaceutical downstream processing in general rather than an in-line dairy whey stream, so the exact magnitude of the thermal effect may differ.
